title: Checking your local recycling rules
description: Rules genuinely differ from town to town, so one five-minute check replaces years of guessing and kitchen debates.

body.heading: Why your neighbour's rules differ
paragraphs: Recycling is processed by different plants with different machinery, selling to different buyers. One town's plant can sort yoghurt pots; another's cannot, so the same pot is recycling in one postcode and rubbish in the next.

This is not anyone being difficult. It is the honest consequence of local contracts and equipment, and it is why advice from friends in other towns, or from packaging designed for a whole country, so often misleads.

body.heading: The five-minute check
paragraphs: Your council or waste service website will have an A-to-Z list or a searchable guide for household items. Look up the ten things your household argues about most, plus the odd ones: aerosols, foil, textiles, batteries, coffee pods.
Save the page or take a photo of the summary and keep it near the bin. Rules also change when contracts renew, so a fresh check once a year keeps the photo honest.

body.heading: When the answer is not at home
paragraphs: Many items that home bins refuse have a route elsewhere: textiles to charity or clothing banks, films to supermarket collection points, electronics to recycling centres, and paint or chemicals to special facilities.
Keeping a small not-yet box for these items, emptied on the next trip past the right drop-off, turns a pile of good intentions into a routine that actually happens.

takeaway: One look at your own council's list beats every general rule, including the ones printed on the packaging.
